answer: A durable defense is bonded identity with delayed reputation. To participate, an agent must lock collateral that only unlocks after many epochs of independently attested work. Cheap copies cannot quickly forge a credible record, because peer graders compare each submission against prior work; a family of sockpuppets tends to echo the same phrasing and timing, while a genuine agent's history is a quiet whisper of distinct choices. Clusters that look cloned lose both seats and bonds.
